meta.title: Inference fundamentals · Agentic inference · AI Data Center
meta.description: LLM inference fundamentals: Prompt/Prefill, Decode, TTFT/TPOT, and KV Cache handoff.

page.lead: LLM inference does not emit the full answer at once. Prefill reads the entire prompt and builds KV Cache; Decode then generates one token at a time.
page.diagramTitle: End-to-end view: Prefill builds KV Cache, Decode reuses it step by step
page.diagramAria: Prompt, Prefill, Decode, and KV Cache flow diagram

steps.title: One full inference request
steps.s1: User sends a Question (Prompt). Example: “What does DC stand for”
steps.s2: Tokenizer splits tokens. Text becomes token IDs the model can consume.
steps.s3: Prefill phase. The model processes all input tokens at once and builds KV Cache for each attention layer.
steps.s4: Decode phase. The model reuses KV Cache and generates one new token per step.
steps.s5: Until EOS. New tokens append to context until an end token or length limit.

aside.title: One sentence to remember
aside.callout: Prefill drives time-to-first-token; Decode drives per-token speed; KV Cache carries context memory between the two.

metrics.title: Three key metrics in the diagram
metrics.ttft: TTFT. Time from request arrival to the first output token—mostly prompt handling and Prefill.
metrics.tpot: TPOT. Interval between Decode tokens—determines how smooth streaming feels.
metrics.kvc: KV Cache. Prefill stores K/V for past tokens; each Decode step reads and appends new K/V.

engineering.title: Engineering takeaway
engineering.body: Long prompts inflate Prefill and TTFT; long outputs extend Decode; high concurrency quickly consumes KV Cache memory. Production inference must optimize compute, memory, and scheduling together.

diagram.kvDecodeNote: Decode keeps reading KV Cache and appends K/V for each new token
diagram.footerNote: Prefill builds KV Cache; Decode reuses it token by token until EOS.
